title: Watch This Overlooked AI Tool Build Me a Business in 23 Minutes
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The video promotes Replit Agent 3, which the host uses and praises throughout. The host explicitly says he does not plan to make Invoice Freely a business.

stated_problem.quote: Now, as a business owner, I know that invoicing software can be a pain, and it's hard to find invoicing software that is specific to a certain industry.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Invoice Freely for contractors
idea.one_liner: A free AI invoicing app for contractors, with proposed revenue from a markup on card processing.
idea.customer: Contractors, especially home service businesses, home builders, roofers, general contractors and subcontractors; potentially any small business issuing invoices.
idea.offer: A web app where customers enter invoice details in natural language by email or mobile chatbot; it creates an invoice with a Stripe payment link and sends it by email.
idea.revenue_model: The proposed model is free invoicing with a markup on Stripe card processing. The host suggests a 3 12% processing fee and retaining half a percent, but reports no actual revenue and says he does not plan to run the business.

key_quotes.quote: So, let's make free invoicing software that's AI enabled and built with AI because we don't know how to code for contractors.
I'm actually going to change that either via email or a chatbot window to create and send invoices that have a Stripe link attached.
So then we can make half a percent of every single scent pushed through our software and then our customers can mark it up or they can just pass it on if they want.
Even if we had a 100 customers on this business, that could be $1,000 a month. That's awesome.
So now I better get some sort of a lead capture, email capture, lead magnet on this because once this video goes live, you might you guys might want to use uh invoice freely.
Am I planning on making this a business? No.

claims.claim: The proposed invoicing software would be free for users.
claims.quote: So, let's make free invoicing software that's AI enabled and built with AI because we don't know how to code for contractors.

claims.claim: The host estimates Stripe charges about 2.9% to process a card payment.
claims.quote: Free to them doesn't necessarily mean unpaid to you or to me because with invoicing software, Stripe is going to charge about 2.9% to process that credit card payment.

claims.claim: He suggests a possible processing fee rendered in the transcript as 3 12%.
claims.quote: So maybe our credit card processing fee is 3 12%.

claims.claim: He suggests retaining half a percent of payment volume, with customers able to pass the fee on or mark it up.
claims.quote: So then we can make half a percent of every single scent pushed through our software and then our customers can mark it up or they can just pass it on if they want.

claims.claim: The host expects Resend's free plan may cover the app's email needs.
claims.quote: I'm pretty sure under their free plan, we can do what we need to do.

claims.claim: The host says a Twilio phone number costs $1 per month for the proposed SMS option.
claims.quote: You're going to buy a phone number in Twilio for $1 a month.

claims.claim: The host says US A2P registration takes about two weeks for the planned SMS option.
claims.quote: Here in the United States, they have what's called A2P registration that takes about 2 weeks.

claims.claim: The host bought an unregistered domain for $11 for the prototype.
claims.quote: It's 11 bucks. I'm going to go ahead and buy it.

claims.claim: The host claims there are 33 million small businesses that need invoicing software and that most are unhappy with it.
claims.quote: There's 33 million small businesses that all need invoicing software and most of them are not happy with it.

claims.claim: He projects that 100 customers could produce $1,000 per month.
claims.quote: Even if we had a 100 customers on this business, that could be $1,000 a month. That's awesome.

claims.claim: He describes the hypothetical revenue as achievable with almost no cost.
claims.quote: That's awesome. With almost no cost.

claims.claim: The app builder estimated that building the app would take more than 20 minutes.
claims.quote: It says it's going to take 20 plus minutes to build the entire app.

claims.claim: The host says he built the prototype in under an hour.
claims.quote: We vibe coded it in under an hour.

claims.claim: A test invoice prompt used an $800 tree-trimming invoice.
claims.quote: Send an invoice to Mary Smith for $800 for tree trimming.

claims.claim: A test email showed an unexplained $150 invoice amount.
claims.quote: But I don't care. I don't know why it's $150.

claims.claim: A test invoice for $400 appeared in the app.
claims.quote: When I go into my resend account and I go to the first tab, emails, I can see that it sent these emails, or at least it's cued. It's queued up to send.

acquisition_channels.details: The host expected viewers of this video might use the app and said he should add lead capture, email capture and a lead magnet. He did not describe an ongoing acquisition plan.

ideas.delivery: Self-serve web app for contractors. Users enter invoice details through email or a mobile-friendly chatbot; the app generates a Stripe checkout link and sends the invoice through Resend. SMS through Twilio is described as a possible later feature, not the tested MVP. The host demoed a prototype, not an operating business.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal data in invoices and customer records. PECR would apply to any later direct marketing; the described lead capture is not unsolicited outreach. No subscription model or employment placement service is described, so DMCC subscription rules and Employment Agencies Regulations are not implicated by the transcript.
